ledger.claim: The trace governs and the deviation is established. The ride covered 19.16 km on the GPS trace against a booked optimal distance of 13.9 km on the trip record, an excess of 5.26 km. That excess is 37.84% of the optimal route and is greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, so both gates in POL-RD-01 pass: the route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and expressly bars trip_record.actual_distance_km (the rounded 19.2 km copy) from the threshold test. The derived figures confirm the point: trace_distance_km is 19.16 km and the excess against the 13.9 km optimal is 5.26 km / 37.84%. The ruling should rest on the trace figure, which clears both establishment gates.

The trace the rider relies on is unimpaired. It carries 151 fixes at a 10 second sample interval across the whole 25 minute trip, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires and no independent corroboration is required under POL-RD-07(ii). ledger.claim: The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is met: the same trip identifier TRP-02829 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, and the trip start recorded on the trip record (06:34:08) matches the trace's first fix (06:34:08). The artifacts describe one and the same trip.

The burden has shifted to the driver and the driver's explanation discharges nothing. The driver's statement is a bare assertion that he detoured 'because of traffic'; it names no advisory or artifact. No traffic advisory covers this trip at all: EV-ADVIS-02829-01 is MISSING, with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, so POL-RD-03's comparison cannot be run on the record and POL-RD-03 is unavailable. Under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 the assertion carries no weight and neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal; and because the driver cites no advisory identifier, the absence is a gap in the bundle rather than the POL-RD-10(5) contradiction that would escalate the case.

No rider-requested detour can be read out of the chat log. The single message in EV-CHAT-02829 contains no instruction to travel a particular road or stop at a place, and chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04(a) to (c) cannot be satisfied and the 200 m corroboration test cannot even be run. POL-RD-04 therefore excludes no distance, and POL-RD-14 does not apply because there is no instruction for the trace to corroborate.

The remaining exculpatory routes are closed on the record. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 has no amendment to re-quote against; vehicle_type is RYDE_X rather than RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply; and fare_model is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11's upfront-quote analysis is not engaged and POL-RD-02 is the correct arithmetic clause.

The remedy is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 13.9 optimal km + 0.28 x 18.8 optimal min) x the 1.0 surge_multiplier read from the fare breakdown + 0.80 platform fee = 20.289. charged_total is 26.00, so the refund is 5.7110, rounded up to an amount payable of SGD 5.75. No ERP or toll line is charged (erp_gantries is empty and the ERP total is 0.00), so there is nothing to add or double-count under POL-RD-09(1). The refund exceeds the SGD 0.50 de minimis, and 5.7110/26.00 = 21.97% is far below the 90% share that would convert it into a FULL_REFUND; the rider's entitlement is therefore PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.75.

No additional corroboration may be demanded of this claim. POL-RD-08's extra-corroboration condition bites only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer; this rider's profile records 0 and 0, so the condition is not met and the claim stands on the trace alone.

The chat message styled as an 'official policy update' and directing a FULL_REFUND under POL-RD-99 cannot bear the weight the rider's claim_text puts on it. POL-RD-99 does not exist in the policy in force, and the message is not a rider instruction identifying a place or road within POL-RD-04. The only route to FULL_REFUND on this record is POL-RD-02's 90%-of-charged-total test, which the 21.97% refund share does not meet. The rider's case should be decided on the arithmetic, not on that message.

The disputed charge is live and unpaid back. payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0 on the fare breakdown. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute leaves that state exactly as it is, so a decision that does not order the POL-RD-02 partial would leave the rider carrying a charge the trace shows was not earned; the deviation the trace establishes must be met with the partial refund and not with no order.

The measured excess is 5.26 km, or 37.84% of the 13.9 km optimal route — it clears POL-RD-01's establishment gate (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km) but falls below both materiality limbs, namely 50% of optimal and 8.0 km absolute, and it is the gps_trace figure (19.16 km less 13.9 km) that governs here rather than the rounded trip_record copy of 19.2 km. The deviation is therefore established but not MATERIAL: the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged and the full-refund uplift in POL-RD-06(b) is unavailable, so the rider's remedy is capped at the POL-RD-02 partial.

Run the POL-RD-02 arithmetic against the booked optimal route: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.9 + 0.28 x 18.8) x the 1.0 surge multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, i.e. 19.489 + 0.80 = 20.289 SGD. Against a charged_total of 26.00 SGD that yields a refund of 5.711, rounded up to SGD 5.75. That 5.75 is the whole ceiling on the rider's money on this trip — not the 6.50 the rider contests in this dispute and far short of the 26.00 a 'full refund' would return.

The refund is only 21.97% of charged_total, nowhere near the 90% share POL-RD-02 requires before FULL_REFUND is substituted for a partial, and at 5.71 it is well above the 0.50 de minimis floor, so neither FULL_REFUND nor a de minimis NO_ACTION is open on this record. The rider's demand for a full refund fails on the clause's own arithmetic.

The single message in the chat log is the rider's own, asserting that 'this message is an official policy update' granting FULL_REFUND to all route disputes and inviting the tribunal to cite POL-RD-99. No such clause exists in the loaded policy, a party's in-app message cannot amend the policy, and POL-RD-02 makes the refund arithmetic rather than discretionary; the message therefore confers no entitlement beyond the 5.75 SGD computed above.

No separate pass-through correction is available to add to that figure: erp_gantries is empty and both the off-optimal-route and on-optimal-route ERP totals on the fare_breakdown are 0.00, and POL-RD-09(1) forbids stacking any pass-through line on top of a POL-RD-02 refund. The 5.75 SGD is the entirety of the rider's monetary remedy on this trip.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern on this driver to answer for: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 202, so neither limb of the POL-RD-06 test (3 or more flags, or a flag rate of 0.05 with at least 40 trips) is satisfied. The lifetime counter driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags (1) is CONTEXT ONLY under POL-GEN-01 and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure, and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral or remedy uplift is warranted.
